title: Memory Systems: Remember Deliberately
objective: After this lesson you will be able to separate episodic, semantic, and working memory; write read/write/decay policies per store; and retrieve with budgets that prevent unbounded growth.
why: 'The agent forgot my preference' and 'the agent remembers everything including noise' are the same missing system: memory without policy. Episodic (what happened), semantic (what's true), and working (what's active) stores with explicit write rules, decay schedules, and retrieval budgets turn remembering from accident into infrastructure — the difference between personalization and landfill.

blocks.text: **Episodic**: event records (tickets, outcomes, timestamps) — append-only, queried by recency/similarity. **Semantic**: facts and preferences (user tier, policy exceptions) — upserted, versioned, contradicted explicitly. **Working**: active task state (Ch.2 budgets apply) — bounded, summarized, discarded on completion. One store for all three confuses jobs: facts need updates, episodes need immutability, working needs bounds.

blocks.caption: Write paths differ per store: append vs versioned-upsert vs bounded-overwrite

blocks.text: Every stored byte needs a retention reason: **recency decay** (untouched episodes fade), **importance floors** (VIP facts persist), **explicit expiry** (session tokens die on schedule). Decay runs as scheduled jobs with logs (what pruned, why) — silent accumulation is the default without them. Contradictions resolve by version (newer wins, old preserved in history) never by silent overwrite.

blocks.caption: Prune with reasons logged: retention as auditable policy

blocks.text: Reads are budgeted like context (they become context): top-k episodic by recency+similarity, semantic by key with version check, working direct. Retrieval caps prevent memory from re-flooding the windows Ch.2 just budgeted — stores without read budgets are just slower context overflow.

blocks.title: Write, decay, retrieve
blocks.note: Run it: semantic tier platinum v2 (versioned upsert, contradiction explicit); decay keeps 1 (VIP importance floor) prunes 1 (aged ordinary). Write paths differ, decay respects floors, versions never silently overwrite.

items: Episodic appends (immutable history), semantic versioned-upserts (contradictions explicit), working bounded-overwrites
Decay by age/importance/expiry with pruned-logs; importance floors protect VIP facts
Retrieval budgeted per store — stores without read caps re-flood managed windows

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice memory and confirm versioning + decay outcomes. (b) Add an expiry rule (session tokens die after 1h regardless of importance) with a test. (c) Write the retrieval budget for a support turn (episodic top-3 + semantic keys + working direct) with caps justified per store.
hints: Baseline: tier platinum v2; kept 1 (VIP floor), pruned 1 (aged ordinary). Versions prove contradiction handling.
Expiry: kind check (session-*) with hard deadline overriding importance floors — security tokens never persist on importance.
Budgets: episodic 3 (recent context), semantic 5 keys (facts cheap), working direct (already bounded) — caps prevent re-flooding.
exercise.why: Versioning (contradictions explicit), expiry overrides (security beats importance), and read budgets (stores can't re-flood windows) are the three memory policies — each enforced, with decay logged.
exercise.code: // Memory-policy pattern: kind-specific writes + floors + expiry + read caps.

quiz.q: Agent cites a superseded preference as current. Root cause + fix?
options: Silent overwrite: semantic updates need versioning (newer wins, history preserved) — contradictions explicit, never overwritten
quiz.explain: Versioned upserts make supersession visible and auditable. Silent overwrites corrupt without trace.

quiz.q: Memory grows 10x quarterly with no policy. Response?
options: Write rules + decay schedules + retrieval budgets + pruned logs — retention reasons per byte, or landfill
quiz.explain: Unbounded growth is policy absence: write criteria, decay by age/importance/expiry, read caps. Every byte needs retention reason.

quiz.q: Session token persists via importance floor. Verdict?
options: Security override: session/expiry rules beat importance floors — tokens die on schedule regardless
quiz.explain: Expiry classes (sessions, secrets) override floors: security deadlines ignore importance. Floors protect facts, never credentials.

summary: Episodic appends, semantic versions, working bounds; decay with floors and expiry overrides; retrieval budgeted. Remembering as infrastructure, not accident.
